MRK.rationale: Merck presents a rare case of near-full alignment across all three pillars on the short side. Pillar 1 (fundamental health & trajectory): Q1 2026 GAAP results show a catastrophic earnings collapse — diluted EPS of -$1.72, operating income of -$3.53B, and net income of -$4.24B — driven by the ~$9B Cidara acquisition charge. While the qual report notes non-GAAP EPS of $2.13 excluding the charge, the GAAP reality is that total equity fell from $51.91B to $45.93B in one quarter, net margin collapsed from ~0.296 to 0.136, and ROE dropped to 0.195. The KEYTRUDA patent cliff in 2028 looms over a company that derives ~half its revenue from a single product. GARDASIL declined 22% in the most recent quarter, and the LITESPARK-012 readout failed. Pillar 2 (valuation vs own history): The stock trades at a trailing P/E of 35.9x as of 2026-07-30, near the top of its 1-year range (11.1x–36.5x), while the forward P/E is ~47x. This is extreme multiple expansion on degraded earnings — the market is paying a historically premium multiple precisely when the 'E' has collapsed. The stock has rallied +17% over the prior quarter to $129.79, near its 251-day high of $135.05, despite the fundamental deterioration. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): The LIPFENDRA FDA approval (2026-07-27) is a genuine positive but is already priced in (stock rallied 5.4% on the news). The next earnings report will be the critical test — if the Cidara charge proves truly one-time and non-GAAP earnings power reasserts, the stock could hold, but the current valuation leaves no margin of safety for any disappointment. The Terns acquisition (~$5.8B IPR&D charge expected) adds further near-term earnings noise. The combination of deteriorating GAAP fundamentals, historically extreme valuation, and patent cliff risk creates a strongly negative setup.
